I am sharing my experience regarding YES Securities, which has necessitated the filing of a formal Arbitration.

1. Exhausted All Internal Channels

Despite escalating these issues through every available level—including Customer Support, the Relationship Management team, the Escalation Desk, and the Office of the CEO—the firm has failed to resolve technical failures or honor specific commercial commitments that resulted in significant financial impact.

2. Discrepancies in Service Logs (Evidence of Systemic Failure)

During a platform freeze where I was unable to manage active positions, the firm provided logs to regulators claiming they attempted to reach me. However, my internal data records show multiple instances of "AGENT_HANGUP_UI" and "PROVIDER_TEMP_FAILURE." This indicates that calls were disconnected at the system/agent level before reaching the client, yet were presented as valid service attempts in their CRM reports to regulators.

3. Breach of Settlement Agreement & Brokerage Discrepancies

Following a documented technical failure, the firm offered a formal compensatory package: ₹6 Crore in free turnover or a ₹1 brokerage waiver for three years/brokerage waiver. The firm is now attempting to unilaterally rescind this agreement, claiming the offer was "non-binding" as it was made by customer support. This position is untenable; the offer was explicitly extended by an Escalation Team Manager acting as an authorized representative of the firm.

4. CGST/SGST and Billing Irregularities

On audit of my trade reports (Apr 2024–July 2025) reveals serious tax and billing irregularities. The data shows inconsistent CGST/SGST splits and miscalculated tax values. These findings are being escalated to the CBIC (GST Portal) and SEBI.

5. Failure of Relationship Management

The Relationship Management team remained non-responsive for an extended period during this crisis. Subsequent responses failed to acknowledge documented platform instability, effectively shifting the burden of system-level failures onto the retail investor.

Conclusion

Based on these documented experiences, there is a clear lack of transparency and a failure to honor financial commitments at the leadership level. I am pursuing formal Arbitration to ensure accountability.
